content.title: About
content.content: Canned chicken is a ready‑to‑eat product made from selected chicken meat that is cooked, sealed in an airtight can, and sterilized. The process preserves nutrients while keeping the meat tender and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned chicken is a staple in military rations and backpacking meals because of its long shelf life.
Cans are typically sterilized at 121 °C for 30‑45 minutes, ensuring microbiological safety.
The product usually contains only meat, without skin or bones, making it easy to incorporate into recipes.
When stored properly, canned chicken can last 3‑5 years.
Some brands add a pinch of salt or mild spices, but many versions are sold plain.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Canned chicken provides about 20‑25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Unlike fried chicken, canned versions contain minimal fat, fitting well into low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken meat is rich in niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6), which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: It supplies iron, phosphorus, and zinc, nutrients needed for blood formation and immune health.

items.title: Convenience
items.content: Ready‑to‑eat nature saves cooking time and simplifies meal preparation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is often added for preservation, so people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Although uncommon, some individuals may be allergic to chicken protein.

items.title: Damaged packaging
items.content: Bulging, leaking, or rusted cans may indicate spoilage and should be discarded.

items.title: Bisphenol A (BPA)
items.content: Older cans may be lined with BPA‑containing resin, which some consider a health concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned chicken can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, pasta, rice or potato dishes, or used as a filling for sandwiches and wraps. It can also be gently warmed in the microwave or a skillet if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry, dark place. After opening, transfer the meat to an airtight container and keep it in the refrigerator, using it within 3‑4 days.
